note: Both sets are nearly identical and share the same strengths (Table 4-1 properties, 10-m monopile OD, 150-m hub height, 0.170 Hz first mode, 0.10–0.13 Hz wave range) and the same weaknesses (three claims for the tower's first natural frequency, one of which reads 0.18 Hz against the text's 0.170 Hz, and figure-derived values supported only by legend labels). Set A is marginally better because it binds the steel Young's modulus and shear modulus to 'tower steel' and keeps the Table 4-1 source condition, whereas Set B uses the vaguer entity 'steel' and drops the condition. Neither set captures the 7% outfitting mass, the 100-t transition piece mass, or the note that a floating/semisubmersible substructure requires a stiffer tower.
remarks: The 0.18 Hz, 0.17 Hz and 0.170 Hz claims are all the same fact (text states 0.170 Hz); the 0.18 Hz value is a misread and the 0.17 Hz claim is a duplicate with a fabricated bracketed quote. Figure-derived values (1P 0.09–0.13 Hz, 3P 0.25–0.38 Hz, JONSWAP peak ~0.11 Hz, Kaimal PSD 1.00 at 0 Hz) are plausible readings of Figure 4-1 but their quotes are only legend labels, which do not support the numbers. Note the source table itself lists 'Pa' as the unit for Poisson's ratio of soil (a document error); both sets correctly omit it. Important facts both sets miss: 7% outfitting mass and 100 t transition piece in final mass values, soil modeled via spring constants representative of dense sand/gravel, and the requirement for a stiffer tower with a floating substructure.
